papers.title_en: ACAM-J-MARS: Multi-Atlas Riemannian Spectral Representations for Decoding Advanced Meditation States from fMRI
papers.authors: Jian Wang, Winson F. Z. Yang, Wugeng Zheng, Matthew D. Sacchet
papers.evidence: 结合黎曼几何的fMRI功能连接分析
papers.tldr: 从fMRI解码高级禅修状态受空间分布效应、个体差异大和小样本困扰，传统欧氏单图谱方法忽略功能连接的非欧几何与时序信息。ACAM-J-MARS用多图谱构建功能连接，将SPD矩阵映射到黎曼流形并对数欧氏切空间投影，再融合低频BOLD谱能量特征。在22名练习者204个片段上，早晚期二分类平衡准确率达0.757，三分类0.545，较最强基线提升10.8个百分点。该表示有望提升高级冥想状态解码，并服务闭环神经反馈与实时脑机接口。
papers.abstract_en: Inferring jhana-type advanced concentration absorption meditation (ACAM-J) states from fMRI data is challenging due to the spatially distributed nature of meditation-related effects, substantial inter-individual variability that can exceed within-subject state differences, and limited sample sizes. Conventional machine-learning approaches often formulate this problem as unimodal, Euclidean, atlas-based classification, thereby neglecting the non-Euclidean geometry of functional connectivity matrices and underrepresenting temporal information in functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI); these limitations can lead to suboptimal classification performance. We propose ACAM-J-MARS (\textbf{M}ulti-\textbf{A}tlas \textbf{R}iemannian \textbf{S}pectral representation), which computes functional connectivity using multiple atlases, represents symmetric positive definite (SPD) connectivity matrices on a Riemannian manifold, projects them into a log-Euclidean tangent space, and augments connectivity-derived features with low-frequency BOLD spectral energy to better resolve subtle state differences under heterogeneous variability. Evaluated on 204 segments from 22 practitioners, ACAM-J-MARS improves performance across multiple backbone models, achieving a balanced accuracy of 0.757 for early versus late ACAM-J classification and 0.545 for three-class classification, corresponding to a 10.8-point absolute improvement over the strongest baseline. These findings suggest that the proposed representation improves the decoding of advanced meditative brain states and may enable downstream applications such as closed-loop neurofeedback and real-time psychophysiological brain-computer interfaces.

papers.title_en: Latent Prediction Yields Cross-Subject Alignable Representations in Sensory-Evoked fMRI
papers.authors: Serwan Jassim, Victoria Bosch, Daniel Anthes, Elia Bruni, Tim Kietzmann
papers.evidence: 基于自监督学习的感官诱发fMRI解码与跨被试对齐表征
papers.tldr: 针对感觉诱发fMRI解码，本文探索自监督学习能否学到强下游表征。作者将JEPA用于仅基于脑数据的受试者专属编码器，不接触刺激图像或其派生表征。在NSD上，脑嵌入用于脑图说与图像重建，性能接近依赖图像和语言端到端训练的监督流程。独立训练的受试者编码器可无监督对齐，对齐后解码头跨受试者免微调迁移并保留大部分性能，为跨受试者汇聚fMRI数据提供新途径。
papers.abstract_en: Decoding sensory-evoked functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data is a central analytical tool in cognitive neuroscience. Here we ask whether self-supervised learning (SSL), which has been scarcely explored in this domain, can yield representations that support strong downstream performance. To do so, we adapt a joint embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) to train participant-specific encoders on brain data alone. The encoders never see the stimulus images or any representation derived from them. Applied to the Natural Scenes Dataset (NSD), we evaluate our learned brain embeddings on the downstream tasks of brain captioning and image reconstruction, as well as cross-participant generalization. Our self-supervised approach achieves competitive performance with parameter-rich supervised pipelines that are trained end-to-end with access to image and language data. We further find that encoders trained independently for different participants can be aligned fully unsupervised, using neither images nor stimuli shared between them. After alignment, a neural decoding head trained on one participant can be applied to another without fine-tuning and retains most of its within-subject performance on image reconstruction and brain captioning. By removing the need for images and shared stimuli, our approach is a step towards pooling fMRI data across participants and, eventually, across datasets.

papers.title_en: L0-Norm-Based CycleGAN for Unpaired Brain CT-to-MR Synthesis
papers.authors: Yunxiao Zhang, Shouqiang Du, Zexian Xu, Chuanlong Xu
papers.evidence: 基于L0范数循环一致性的脑CT到MR合成
papers.tldr: 脑部CT与MR信息互补，但临床中常难以同时获取；CycleGAN可实现无配对CT到MR合成，然而L1循环一致性惩罚对大残差更敏感，易忽略小残差。本文用平滑有界函数近似L0范数作为循环一致性项，增强对小残差的约束并抑制大残差影响。在102幅训练、9幅测试图像上，MSE降低20.7%，PSNR和SSIM均优于基线。结果表明改进惩罚项能提升重建精度。
papers.abstract_en: Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance (MR) imaging provide complementary information for the brain, but acquiring both modalities is not always possible. The cycle-consistent adversarial network (CycleGAN) enables unpaired CT-to-MR synthesis, but because the standard L1-norm cycle?consistency penalty grows linearly with the residual magnitude, the network tends to focus on large residuals. This paper introduces an L0-norm-based cycle?consistency term, in which the L0-norm is approximated by a smooth and bounded function. This approximation not only increases sensitivity to small residuals but also effectively suppresses the influence of large residuals. The proposed model and an otherwise identical L1-norm baseline were trained on 102 images and evaluated on 9 test images. The proposed model achieves a lower mean squared error (0.02746 versus 0.03464, a 20.7% reduction), a higher mean peak signal-to-noise ratio (15.80 versus 14.77 dB), and a higher mean structural similarity index (0.5689 versus 0.5407). It also has a lower maximum MSE and higher minimum PSNR and SSIM than the baseline. These results indicate that modifying the cycle-consistency penalty can improve reconstruction accuracy on this dataset.

papers.title_en: Data Amount Heterogeneity Improves Performance in Federated Learning for Neuroimaging
papers.authors: Paul Kurian, Tamoghna Chattopadhyay, Abhijith Shaji, Greg Ver Steeg, Paul M. Thompson, Jose Luis Ambite
papers.evidence: 用于神经影像阿尔茨海默病分类的联邦学习
papers.tldr: 联邦学习可在不共享神经影像数据的前提下训练阿尔茨海默病分类模型，但真实联盟中各站点数据量差异明显。本文比较数据量异质联邦（一个大站点加多个小站点）与同质联邦的训练表现。结果显示，异质联邦在低数据场景下更优，大站点带来更快收敛和更高最终准确率，并接近集中训练。该发现说明应利用站点间数据量差异，提升大型联盟中小数据站点的价值。
papers.abstract_en: Federated Learning (FL) allows for secure analysis of distributed data without data sharing. We and others have successfully applied FL to neuroimaging tasks, such as Alzheimer's disease classification from structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). FL trains a deep learning model locally at each site, encrypts the local model parameters and sends them to a federation controller that aggregates the local models under homomorphic encryption, the resulting community model is sent back to the sites for further training, and the process repeats for a number of rounds. FL often achieves learning performance (e.g., accuracy) close to centralized training, but no data leaves the sites and model parameters are protected through encryption and other measures.   In this paper, we show that federations composed of sites with heterogeneous amounts of data (1 large site plus small sites) perform better than homogeneous (same data per site) federations, particularly in low data regimes, while reaching performance close to centralized training. Having a big site often results in faster convergence and higher final accuracy. Heterogeneous federations better exploit sites with small amounts of data, a common situation in large consortia such as ENIGMA.
